Modified assessment incorporating the Financial Stability Report (FSR):
- Macro backdrop remains supportive: strong labor markets and solid household spending, with inflation running below target and a flat Phillips curve supporting an unchanged policy rate.
- FSR lens adds caution: elevated nonfinancial corporate leverage (including leveraged loans and a large BBB segment) increases downside amplification risk in a slowdown; signs of household credit strain in credit card delinquencies contrast with solid net worth; September-style money market fragilities necessitate ongoing T-bill purchases and repo operations to maintain ample reserves and smooth policy transmission.
- Policy implementation steps (bill purchases, repos, reinvestments) align with FSR-identified funding-market vulnerabilities and should help contain spillovers.

Net tone: supportive stance amid strong labor data and low inflation, but more cautious than a purely macro read would suggest due to elevated corporate credit vulnerabilities and short-term funding risks highlighted in the FSR.

Representative line: “Job gains have been solid… and the unemployment rate has remained low,” but “business fixed investment and exports remain weak,” and the Fed’s continued T-bill purchases and repo operations reflect attention to funding-market vulnerabilities noted in the FSR.
